algorithm.name: facecap-inspired-v2-strict
algorithm.note: joint identity, reliable open lower-face correction, batched fixed-ray acceptance, safe Loop prior

rebuild.note: P0 fast path: no standard/larynx renders and no display-only result/ duplicates by default; --render and --no-minimal-output restore the verbose path. final/, measured/, quick_check.json, run_report.json and the dense parameters.npz/reference_geometry.json are always kept.

neck_prominence.note: 0.9.0 public default = reference_driven_neck_volume (head_rgbd/neck_volume.py): ONE unified low-frequency cross-section-driven neck volume field rebuilds the whole neck, head/neck and neck/shoulder transitions from the unshaped baseline. The old two-feature continuous_reference path (neck_dual) is retained only as a historical/CLI option: its narrow front ROI, stacked non-negative fields and local peak subdivision were the source of the ring grooves, step ridges and longitudinal facets. The head scale is corrected with a traceable menton (H ratio ~1.01, NOT 1.6368). editing_mode=true, geometry_source=reference_driven_neck_volume, subject_observation_matched=false.
neck_prominence.proportional_note: proportional sizing (0.5.7 candidate, tools/run_neck_proportional.py) is available but NOT the default: W10/W_neck and L50/W50 did not meet the project preference on this short-neck template; see docs/NECK_PROPORTIONAL_SCULPT_REPORT.html. amplitude_mm/candidate_amplitudes_mm apply ONLY to --neck-algorithm observation (research path); the default manual_edit size is the fixed 5 mm design.
neck_prominence.continuous_note: historical 0.6/0.7 path only. The public 0.9 default falls back to the unshaped baseline (status skipped) if the reference is missing or the volume guard audit fails; it never falls back to any old local bump design.
neck_prominence.two_feature_note: historical 0.7.0 path. The project-owned reference copy assets/neck_reference/identity_rest_20261109.obj (source SHA 2e334111...) is shared by the 0.9 volume default.
neck_prominence.volume_note: 0.9: cross-section targets are expressed in head-normalised coordinates and adapted to the target neck length and existing shoulder/chest extent; controlled inward (mid neck) and outward (root) motion are both allowed; the bottom cut ring is anchored with bounded in-plane adjustment; closed/open share one design through vertex correspondence; consistent 1->4 subdivision re-solves positions from the smooth target contour.
